She asked, "Where do you live?" → She asked me ____.
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
items.why: 간접화법으로 바꿀 때 '의문사 + 주어 + 동사' 순서가 되고, 시제는 과거(lived)로 맞춰요.

items.q: He said to me, "What are you doing?" 를 간접화법으로 바꾼 것은?
o: He asked me what was I doing.
He asked me what I be doing.
He asked me what did I do.
He asked me what I was doing.
items.why: 의문문을 전달할 때는 asked를 쓰고 what 뒤에 '주어 + 동사'를 쓰며, 시제를 과거(was doing)로 맞춰요.

items.q:
Do you know ____ is calling you?
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
items.why: is calling의 주어가 필요하므로 주격 의문대명사 who가 알맞아요.

items.q: 모르는 사람에게 시간을 정중하게 묻는 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
o: Hey, tell me what time it is right now.
Excuse me, do you know what time it is?
What time is it? I need to know it now!
Tell me the time now, please hurry up.
items.why: 모르는 사람에게는 'Excuse me, do you know ...'처럼 간접의문문으로 묻는 것이 정중해요.

items.q:
I wonder ____ the answer is correct.
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
items.why: '답이 맞는지'라는 뜻이므로 '~인지 아닌지'를 뜻하는 if가 알맞아요.

items.q: 다음 중 의문사 바로 뒤에 do/does/did를 써야 하는 문장은?
o: Do you know where your sister works?
I don't know where your sister works.
Tell me where your sister works.
items.why: 직접 의문문에만 do/does/did가 필요해요. 간접의문문에서는 where your sister works처럼 평서문 어순을 써요.

items.q: 그 영화가 재미있는지 궁금해요. → I wonder ____.
items.why: '~인지'는 whether/if로 이끌고 그 뒤는 '주어 + 동사'예요. that은 의문의 뜻이 없어요.

items.q:
Can you tell me ____ the party begins?
(시간을 묻는 말)
items.why: 시간을 묻는 의문사는 when이에요.

items.q:
I want to know why ____.
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
items.why: why 뒤에는 '주어 + 동사' 순서가 와요.

items.q: 간접의문문에 대한 설명으로 옳은 것은?
o: 의문사 뒤에 항상 do, does, did를 쓴다.
items.why: 간접의문문은 의문사 + 주어 + 동사 순서이고 do/does/did를 쓰지 않아요. 문장 끝 부호는 전체 문장에 따라 달라요.

items.q:
다음 우리말을 영어로 옮긴 것은?
누가 이 창문을 깼는지 말해 주세요.
o: Please tell me who this window broke.
Please tell me who does break this window.
Please tell me who broke this window.
Please tell me who breaking this window.
items.why: who가 주어이므로 who 바로 뒤에 동사 broke를 쓰고, do/does는 쓰지 않아요.

items.q:
I wonder how many books ____.
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
items.why: how many books 뒤에 '주어 + 동사' 순서(Jinho has read)로 써요.

items.q:
다음 우리말을 영어로 옮긴 것은?
너는 그녀가 몇 시에 올 거라고 생각하니?
o: What time do you think she will come?
Do you think what time she will come?
What time you think she will come?
Do you think what time will she come?
items.why: think 같은 동사가 있으면 의문사를 맨 앞에 두고 'do you think + 주어 + 동사' 순서로 써요.

items.q: know, wonder, ask 뒤에서 '~인지 아닌지'라는 뜻으로 쓸 수 있는 두 단어는?
items.why: 예/아니요로 답하는 질문을 간접의문문으로 만들 때 if나 whether를 써요.

items.q:
She didn't tell me ____ she was upset. (이유)
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
items.why: 이유를 나타내는 의문사는 why예요.

items.q: I don't know what to do. 와 뜻이 같은 문장은?
o: I don't know what I did.
I don't know what I should do.
I don't know what I did not do.
I don't know what did I do.
items.why: 의문사 + to부정사는 '의문사 + 주어 + should + 동사원형'과 같은 뜻이에요.

items.q: 길을 물을 때 어법상 옳은 문장은?
o: I'd like to know how I can get to the station.
I'd like to know how can I get to the station.
I'd like to know how to I can get the station.
I'd like to know how I can getting to the station.
items.why: 간접의문문의 어순은 '의문사 + 주어 + 조동사 + 동사원형'이에요.

items.q: 도서관에 관한 네 문장 중 틀린 문장은?
o: Do you know when the library closes on Sundays?
Please tell me where the new library is.
I wonder if the library is open today.
Do you know when does the library close?
items.why: when does the library close는 직접 의문문 어순이에요. when the library closes로 써야 해요.

items.q: She asked me, "Do you like jazz?" → She asked me ____ I liked jazz.
items.why: 예/아니요 질문을 전달할 때는 if나 whether를 써요.

items.q: 'Nobody knows ____ will win the contest.' 에서 who의 역할은?
items.why: who는 will win의 주어 역할을 해서 바로 뒤에 동사구가 와요.

items.q: When did the bridge open? → Who can tell me ____?
items.why: 간접의문문에서 did를 없애고 동사를 과거형(opened)으로 써요.

items.q: My mom asked, "Have you eaten?" → My mom asked me ____.
items.why: yes/no 질문은 whether/if + 주어 + 동사로 전달하고, 시제를 과거 쪽으로 맞춰 had eaten으로 써요.

items.q: 다음 중 간접의문문이 들어 있는 문장은?
o: Why are you smiling so happily today?
You are smiling a lot more than usual.
Tell me why you are smiling.
Please stop smiling at me right now.
items.why: Tell me why you are smiling에서 why you are smiling이 간접의문문이에요.

items.q: 여행자가 쓴 네 문장 중 틀린 문장이 있는 것은?
o: Do you know where the ticket office is?
Can you tell me where do I buy tickets?
I wonder how much a ticket costs.
Please tell me when the train leaves.
items.why: where do I buy는 직접 의문문 어순이에요. where I buy tickets로 써야 해요.

items.q: 수학여행에 관해 쓴 문장 중 옳은 것은?
o: I don't know when we will leave.
I don't know when will we leave.
I don't know when we leaves.
I don't know when we will leaving.
items.why: when 뒤에 '주어 + will + 동사원형' 순서예요.

items.q: 전화 통화에 관한 문장 중 틀린 문장이 있는 것은?
o: I wonder who is calling me.
Tell me who she is calling.
She asked me who was at the door.
Do you know who is she calling?
items.why: 목적어인 who 뒤에는 '주어 + 동사'가 와야 하므로 who she is calling이 맞아요. who is calling me의 who는 주어예요.

items.q: 잃어버린 지갑에 관한 문장 중 옳은 것은?
o: Do you remember where did you lose it?
Do you remember where you lose it did?
Do you remember where you lost it?
Do you remember where lost you it?
items.why: where 뒤에 '주어 + 동사' 순서이고, 과거의 일이므로 lost를 써요.

items.q: 라디오 진행자의 말 중 옳은 문장은?
o: We don't know whether will it snow tonight.
We don't know whether it will snow tonight.
We don't know whether it snows will tonight.
We don't know whether snow it will tonight.
items.why: whether 뒤에 '주어 + will + 동사원형'을 써요.

items.q: 음식에 관한 문장 중 옳은 것은?
o: She asked how the soup tasted.
She asked how did the soup taste.
She asked how tasted the soup.
She asked how the soup taste.
items.why: how 뒤에 '주어 + 동사'를 쓰고 시제는 과거(tasted)로 맞춰요.

items.q:
A: Do you know ____?
B: Yes, it's on Main Street. 빈칸에 알맞은 것은? (A는 빵집 위치를 묻는다)
items.why: 'where + 주어 + be동사' 순서가 간접의문문이에요.

items.q:
A: I wonder ____.
B: Let's ask the teacher. She will know.
o: what is the answer to number five
what the answer to number five be
what the answer to number five is
items.why: what 뒤에 '주어 + be동사' 순서를 써요.

items.q:
A: Excuse me. Do you know ____?
B: Yes, the post office is next to the bank.
items.why: B의 대답이 위치이므로 where이 알맞고, 어순은 where the post office is예요.

items.q: 다음 중 의문사가 있지만 의문문이 아닌 문장은?
o: I don't know where she went.
Where did she go after school?
Who is the girl in the red coat?
What does she want for lunch?
items.why: I don't know where she went는 평서문이고 where she went는 간접의문문이에요.

items.q: Could you tell me ____? 에 들어갈 수 없는 것은?
items.why: 간접의문문에는 do/does를 쓰지 않아요. where does the bus stop은 직접 의문문 어순이에요.

items.q:
다음 우리말을 영어로 옮긴 것은?
그녀는 우리에게 빵 굽는 방법을 보여 주었다.
o: She showed us how baking bread.
She showed us to how bake bread.
She showed us how to bake bread.
She showed us how we baking bread.
items.why: how to + 동사원형은 '~하는 방법'이에요.

items.q:
I have no idea ____ to turn off the machine.
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
items.why: '기계를 끄는 방법'이므로 how to가 알맞아요.

items.q: I don't know what I should say. 와 같은 뜻의 문장은?
o: I don't know what to say.
I don't know to say what.
I don't know what for say.
items.why: what I should say는 what to say로 줄여 쓸 수 있어요.

items.q:
She wondered ____ the bus was late.
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
items.why: '버스가 늦는지'라는 뜻이므로 whether가 알맞아요.

items.q:
다음 문장의 끝에 알맞은 문장부호는?
Do you know when the festival begins___
items.why: Do you know ...로 시작하는 문장은 직접 묻는 문장이므로 물음표로 끝나요.

items.q:
다음 문장의 끝에 알맞은 문장부호는?
I wonder when the festival begins___
items.why: I wonder ...는 평서문이므로 마침표로 끝나요.

items.q: 다음 중 문장 끝에 물음표(?)를 써야 하는 것은?
o: Can you tell me where the exit is
Please tell me where the exit is
I know where the exit is
She asked where the exit was
items.why: Can you tell me ...는 정중하게 묻는 의문문이므로 물음표로 끝나요. 나머지는 평서문이나 요청문이에요.

items.q: What does he do on Sundays? → Do you know ____?
o: what does he do on Sundays
what he does do on Sundays
items.why: does를 없애고 동사에 -s를 붙여 what he does on Sundays로 써요.

items.q: Who is that man? → I'd like to know ____.
items.why: 'who + 주어 + be동사' 순서가 돼요.

items.q: Could you tell me ____ many people live in your town?
items.why: 수를 묻는 how many를 이루려면 how가 필요해요.

items.q: I wonder ____ kind of pet you have.
items.why: what kind of는 '어떤 종류의'라는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 가장 정중하게 화장실의 위치를 묻는 표현은?
o: Tell me where the restroom is.
Could you tell me where the restroom is?
items.why: Could you tell me ...?처럼 간접의문문을 쓰면 더 정중하게 들려요.

items.q:
다음 문장에서 어색한 부분을 고친 문장은?
I don't know where does Tom live.
o: I don't know where Tom live.
I don't know where did Tom live.
I don't know where Tom lives.
I don't know where lives Tom.
items.why: does를 없애고 Tom lives처럼 '주어 + 동사' 순서로 써요.

items.title: A Lost Dog
items.text: Last Saturday, I found a small brown dog near the park. It wore a blue collar, but there was no name on it. I did not know whose dog it was, so I made a poster. It said, "Do you know who owns this dog? Please call me." I also asked the neighbors whether they had seen it before. An old man told me where a similar dog had lived. We walked to the house together. A girl opened the door and cried with joy. She had been looking for her dog for two days, and I was glad that I could help.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why the writer decided to adopt a brown dog
How the writer helped a lost dog find its home
How a girl taught her dog to open doors
Where neighbors usually walk their dogs in the park
qs.why: 글쓴이가 길 잃은 개를 발견해 주인을 찾아 준 이야기예요.

qs.q: What did the writer's poster say?
o: It asked who owned the dog.
It gave the name of the dog.
It offered a prize to the finder.
It said the dog needed a new home.
qs.why: 포스터에는 'Do you know who owns this dog?'라고 쓰여 있었어요.

qs.q: Who told the writer about the house where a similar dog had lived?
qs.why: An old man told me where a similar dog had lived.

qs.q: What can we infer about the girl?
o: She wanted to give the dog away.
She did not know the old man.
She had been worried about her dog.
She often went to the park at night.
qs.why: 이틀 동안 개를 찾았고 개를 보고 기뻐서 울었으므로 걱정했음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the last sentence, "glad" is closest in meaning to ...
qs.why: glad는 '기쁜'이라는 뜻이라 happy와 가장 가까워요.

items.title: An Email to the Guide
items.text:
Dear Ms. Park,
Our class will visit your science museum next month. Before we come, I have a few questions. Could you tell me what time the museum opens? We also wonder whether students can take photos inside. Our teacher would like to know how long the tour takes, because we must return to school by three o'clock. Finally, please let us know where we can eat lunch. Thank you for your help.
Sincerely,
Jiho Kim, Class 3-2

qs.q: Why did Jiho write this email?
o: To thank the staff for a recent tour
To change the date of a school event
To ask for a job at the museum
To get information before a class visit
qs.why: Jiho는 방문 전에 궁금한 점을 묻기 위해 이메일을 썼어요.

qs.q: What must the class do by three o'clock?
qs.why: we must return to school by three o'clock라고 했어요.

qs.q: Which question does the email NOT ask?
qs.why: 입장권 가격은 묻지 않았어요. 나머지는 모두 본문에 있어요.

qs.q: In the email, "tour" most likely means ...
o: a guided walk around a place
qs.why: how long the tour takes는 박물관을 안내받으며 둘러보는 시간을 뜻해요.

qs.q: Why does Jiho ask how long the tour takes?
o: The class wants to buy souvenirs.
The teacher is afraid of the guide.
The class has a time to get back to school.
qs.why: 3시까지 학교로 돌아와야 해서 투어 시간이 궁금한 거예요.

items.title: Why I Joined the Photo Club
items.text: At first, I did not know why my friend Yuna loved photography. I thought it was just pressing a button. Then I joined the school photo club. The teacher showed us how to find good light and how to choose a subject. Every week we walked around town and took pictures of ordinary things: a bus stop, an old bridge, a woman selling flowers. Now I understand what Yuna meant. A photo can show how a place feels, not only what it looks like. I still make mistakes, but I always wonder what I will notice next.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Buses and bridges are the best subjects for photos
Joining the club changed how the writer sees photos
Yuna wants the writer to buy a new camera
The teacher plans a long trip for the club
qs.why: 글쓴이는 사진부에 들어가 사진을 보는 눈이 달라졌어요.

qs.q: What did the club members do every week?
o: They sold flowers at a market.
qs.why: Every week we walked around town and took pictures.

qs.q: How did the writer's idea about photography change?
o: It changed from liking it to finding it boring.
It changed from loving it to wanting a new hobby.
It changed from fearing cameras to owning many.
It changed from thinking it was simple to seeing more in it.
qs.why: 처음에는 단추만 누르는 일로 생각했지만 나중에는 장소의 느낌까지 담을 수 있다고 이해했어요.

qs.q: "Ordinary" in the passage is closest in meaning to ...
qs.why: 버스 정류장 같은 흔한 것들이므로 ordinary는 usual(평범한)과 가까워요.

qs.q: How does the writer feel at the end?
qs.why: I always wonder what I will notice next에서 호기심을 알 수 있어요.

items.title: The Robot Vacuum
items.text: My family bought a robot vacuum last month. At first, my little brother was afraid of it. He kept asking, "How does it know where to go?" My father explained that small sensors help the robot find walls and chairs. Then my brother asked whether it could clean his room too. We tried it, and the robot stopped in front of his toy box. It could not decide what to do next, so it beeped. My brother laughed and picked up the toys. Since then, he cleans up before the robot starts, and our floor stays much cleaner.

qs.q: What is the best title for the passage?
o: A Boy Who Fears All Machines
How Sensors Are Made in Factories
The Best Toys for Small Children
Learning to Live with a Robot Vacuum
qs.why: 로봇청소기를 들인 뒤 가족이 생활하는 방식을 다룬 이야기예요.

qs.q: How does the robot find walls and chairs?
o: With a map on a phone
qs.why: My father explained that small sensors help the robot find walls and chairs.

qs.q: Why does the brother now clean up before the robot starts?
o: His father punished him for leaving toys.
The robot stopped at his toys and could not go on.
The robot broke the toy box last month.
He wants the robot to clean his toys.
qs.why: 로봇이 장난감 앞에서 멈춘 일이 계기가 되었어요.

qs.q: How did the brother feel when the robot beeped?
qs.why: My brother laughed에서 재미있어했음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: What does the word "it" refer to in "It could not decide what to do next"?
qs.why: it은 앞 문장에서 toy box 앞에 멈춘 로봇청소기를 가리켜요.

items.title: A Visit to the Doctor
items.text: Mr. Han went to the clinic because he felt tired all the time. The doctor asked him many questions. She wanted to know how many hours he slept and what he usually ate for dinner. She also asked whether he exercised regularly. Mr. Han answered that he slept five hours and often ate instant noodles late at night. He did not exercise at all. The doctor smiled and said, "Your body is not sick. It is asking for better habits." She told him to sleep earlier, eat more vegetables, and walk for thirty minutes every day. Two weeks later, he felt much better.

qs.q: Why did Mr. Han go to the clinic?
o: He felt tired all the time.
He needed a paper for work.
qs.why: because he felt tired all the time

qs.q: What did the doctor NOT ask about?
qs.why: 의사는 수면 시간, 저녁 식사, 운동에 대해 물었고 직업은 묻지 않았어요.

qs.q: What does the doctor mean by "It is asking for better habits"?
o: His body needs a stronger medicine.
He should buy new exercise clothes.
He is too busy to see a doctor.
His daily habits are causing his problem.
qs.why: 몸이 아픈 것이 아니라 생활 습관이 문제라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Which advice did the doctor give?
o: Walk for thirty minutes every day
qs.why: walk for thirty minutes every day

qs.q: What happened after Mr. Han followed the advice?
qs.why: Two weeks later, he felt much better.

items.title: At the Airport
items.text: Emma arrived at a big airport for the first time. She could not find her gate, so she asked a staff member, "Excuse me, could you tell me where Gate 14 is?" The woman pointed to a long hallway and said, "Go straight, and you will see a sign." Emma also wanted to know whether the shops were open at that hour. The woman checked her watch and answered that most of them stayed open until midnight. Emma thanked her and walked on. She was nervous, but she felt calmer now because she knew exactly what to do.

qs.q: Why did Emma speak to the staff member?
o: She wanted to change her seat.
She could not find her gate.
qs.why: She could not find her gate, so she asked a staff member.

qs.q: What did the woman tell Emma to do?
o: Take the stairs to the second floor
Go straight and look for a sign
qs.why: Go straight, and you will see a sign.

qs.q: What does "them" refer to in "most of them stayed open"?
qs.why: them은 바로 앞에서 말한 shops를 가리켜요.

qs.q: How did Emma feel at the end?
qs.why: she felt calmer now

qs.q: What can we infer from the passage?
o: Emma likes shopping more than traveling.
Emma was late for her flight.

items.title: Grandma's Soup
items.text: Every winter, my grandmother makes rice cake soup for the whole family. When I was little, I always asked her what the secret was. She would only smile and say, "Time and patience." Last year she finally let me help in the kitchen. She showed me how to slice the rice cakes thinly and when to add the egg. I was surprised that the recipe was so simple. The soup did not taste exactly like hers, though. Grandma laughed and said that I needed a few more winters to learn her secret. I hope she is right.

o: A family trip planned for winter
The writer learning to cook from a grandmother

items.title: The Beach Clean-up
items.text: Our town held a beach clean-up on Sunday morning. About fifty volunteers came, and each person received a bag and a pair of gloves. A leader explained how to separate plastic, glass, and cans. At first, Minjun wondered why they were collecting such small pieces. Then he saw how much trash was hidden in the sand. By noon, the group had filled sixty bags. A volunteer asked everyone to think about where the trash came from. Many of them agreed that people should throw away their trash more carefully. Minjun decided to bring his own bag next time.

items.title: Camping Weather
items.text: Dan and his cousins went camping in the mountains. On the second evening, the sky turned dark, and one cousin asked, "Do you think it will rain tonight?" Nobody could say for sure. Dan remembered that his father had taught him how to read the clouds. He looked at the thick, gray clouds in the west and said they probably meant rain. They quickly moved the bags into the tent and tied the cover tightly. An hour later, the rain began. Everyone stayed dry, and they listened to the drops while they played cards. Dan felt proud of himself.

items.title: The Lunch Survey
items.text: The student council wanted to find out what students thought about the school lunch. They asked three hundred students how often they ate in the cafeteria and which menu they liked best. The results were interesting. Most students ate there four or five days a week, but only a few liked the fish dishes. Many students wrote that they did not know what was in some meals. The council decided to put a menu board with food information outside the cafeteria. They also plan to ask the cooks whether they can offer a vegetable choice on Fridays. The principal said the idea was worth trying.
